turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the repository structure and streaming implementation using the gh CLI without cloning locally.Now let's check `responses/responses.ts` and `client.ts` for how `stream: body.stream` connects to `defaultParseResponse`, plus check ResponseStream, ChatCompletionStream, AssistantStream implementations.Now let's check the beta/threads/runs.ts (assistants API) and audio/speech.ts for streaming, plus the `client.ts` request path and `ResponseStream.ts` / `ChatCompletionStream.ts` implementations.Now let's check ChatCompletionStream, ResponseStream, AssistantStream, and EventStream implementations for their structure.I have enough evidence. Let me also quickly verify the audio/speech.ts binary streaming path and beta/realtime websocket path to be thorough.Good, that gives a complete list. Let me quickly check the two I haven't confirmed yet (transcriptions, threads, completions, images) for their `stream` methods.## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE engine:** `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `Stream<Item>` class — implements `AsyncIterable<Item>`, wraps a `fetch` `Response`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses a `Response` into a stream of items using the private generator `_iterSSEMessages()`.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — alternate constructor for newline-delimited JSON streams (no SSE framing).
- Helper `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / class `SSEDecoder` — do the actual byte-by-byte SSE parsing (splitting on double newlines, decoding `event:`/`data:` fields).
- `src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export (`export * from './core/streaming'`).

**Where the SSE engine gets invoked:** `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse()`. This is the response body parser used by every API call. When `FinalRequestOptions.stream` is truthy, it calls either:
- `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` if a resource specified a custom stream class, or
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (the default) otherwise.

This is wired into `src/core/api-promise.ts`'s `APIPromise<T>`, which lazily calls `parseResponse` (defaulting to `defaultParseResponse`) against the pending `responsePromise`.

**Higher-level "helper" stream wrappers** (built on top of `Stream`, adding event-emitter ergonomics and accumulation/parsing):
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — base class `EventStream<EventTypes>`, generic pub/sub + `AbortController` + connect/end promise plumbing shared by the helpers below.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream`, extends `EventStream`, accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk`s into snapshots, emits `content`, `chunk`, `tool_calls.function.arguments.delta`, etc. Static entry point `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner`, adds automatic tool-call execution on top of `ChatCompletionStream` (`.runTools()`).
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream`, same idea for the Responses API; static `ResponseStream.createResponse()`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream`, same idea for the Assistants (`beta.threads.runs`) API; statics `createAssistantStream()` / `createToolAssistantStream()`.

**A separate, non-SSE streaming path** exists for realtime/WebSocket: `src/resources/realtime/*` and `src/resources/responses/ws.ts` + `ws-base.ts` (`ResponsesWS`) use the `ws` package / browser WebSocket rather than `Stream`/SSE. I did not verify this path in depth — flagging it as architecturally distinct from the SSE `Stream<Item>` mechanism described above.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

Confirmed by grepping every file under `src/resources/**` for imports of `core/streaming` or use of `__streamClass` (7 files matched):

| Resource method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:70-80` | sets `stream: body.stream ?? false` on the request → `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` via `defaultParseResponse` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(...)` | same file, `:221-225` | calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()` directly |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true})` | same file, `:196-212` | delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools()` |
| `client.completions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-41` | → `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | → `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve({stream: true})` | same file, `:144-168` | → `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` (resuming/polling a stream by id) |
| `client.responses.stream(...)` | same file, `:201-205` | calls `ResponseStream.createResponse()` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:68-80` | → `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` (and deprecated `.createAndStream`) | same file, `:163-233` | calls `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs(...).stream` / `submitToolOutputsStream` | same file, `:290-299` | calls `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream()` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream: true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:143-160` | → `Stream<Run>` events |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | same file, `:182` | calls `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:31-62` | → `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream: true})` / `client.images.edit({stream: true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:58,91` | → `Stream<ImageGenPartialEvent>` |

All of the above set `stream: body.stream ?? false` in the options object passed to `this._client.post(...)`, which returns an `APIPromise<T>`; resolving/awaiting/iterating it triggers `defaultParseResponse` in `src/internal/parse.ts`, which is the single choke point that calls into `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (`src/core/streaming.ts`).

`client.audio.speech.create()` (`src/resources/audio/speech.ts:29-35`) is a different, simpler case: it sets `__binaryResponse: true` and returns the raw `Response` object for the caller to read (`response.body`), not the SSE `Stream<Item>` machinery — worth noting so it isn't conflated with the others.

## What I did not verify
- The WebSocket-based realtime streaming code (`src/resources/realtime/*`, `src/resources/responses/ws.ts`, `internal/ws*.ts`) — confirmed it exists and is architecturally separate, but did not trace its internals.
- I did not read every line of the larger files (`completions.ts` is ~2400 lines, `responses.ts` is ~8000+ lines) — line numbers cited are from the sections I fetched and grepped; the repo is generated by Stainless from an OpenAPI spec so line numbers will shift between commits.
- I worked against `main` at the time of inspection (commit visible in the code-search result: `71d2347c...`); did not check whether this differs from the latest published npm release.
